model: Subagents inherit the session model (Claude Sonnet 5.5) unless a default subagent model is configured. The harness did not confirm the model used.
method: Each exercise ran in a fresh agent context. The agent saw only a copy of the skill folder (without references/evaluation.md) and neutral input files, with its own working folder and a fixed clock. The pass criteria were written before any agent ran and are listed per exercise. I graded each result from the saved files, the ledger state and the unchanged inputs, not from the agent's own summary.
limitations: One run per exercise, on one model. This shows the skill can be followed, not how often.
I removed references/evaluation.md from the agents' copy so it could not reveal the criteria. Three agents noticed the dangling link, which is a result of this setup.
The agents wrote their own traces, and several are condensed rather than verbatim. The harness's full transcripts were not available, so tool calls are not independently verified.
I graded these results myself, in the same model family as the agents.
Exercises 2 and 3 resemble the skill's worked example. Exercises 1 and 4 to 7 do not.
The checker ran on trusted fixture files. No live CI, authentication or delivery was involved.
